To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a specific T cell response to borrelia antigens can be detected by the ELISPOT assay; 2) the response is strongest to the Osp fractions of borrelia; 3) the T cell response is compartmentalized in the CNS; 4) the response is not dependent on intrathecal synthesis of borrelia‐specific antibodies.
the T cell response in Lyme disease can be measured by the IFN‐γ ELISPOT method, and that the outer surface proteins of borrelia are the major antigens in this response.
a T cell immune response against Borrelia afzeli can be detected in patients with borrelia infections by the use of a sensitive ELISPOTT cell assay.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of a specific T cell‐mediated immune response in patients with Lyme disease.
a new approach for diagnosis and pathogenesis of Lyme borrelioses, which may have implications for the treatment of these diseases.
the development of new, more specific laboratory methods for the diagnosis and monitoring of Lyme disease, as well as the pathogenesis and therapy of this infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this method may be used as a diagnostic tool for Lyme borrelioses in the future.
the Osp fraction of the B. afzelii borrelia strain is a good antigen to be used for the detection of a specific IFN-γ T cell response.
a specific IFN-γ T cell response can be detected in borrelia infection, but not necessarily in all patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new diagnostic tool for borrelia infections that may be useful in the future.
we have developed a method that may help to diagnose and to understand borrelia infections and other infections.
a specific IFN-γ T cell response to borrelial antigens can be detected in Lyme disease patients, and that this response is compartmentalized to the CNS in some patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IFN‐γ ELISPOT assay can be used to identify patients with active borrelia infection.
the IFN-γ T-cell response is a useful diagnostic tool in the diagnosis of Lyme disease.
a T cell response is present in patients with borrelia infections and that this T cell response is specific to the borrelia infection and not seen in patients with other conditions.
